title: Air Filter Maintenance Checklist for Screw Compressors

text.content: Why the air filter matters

rich_text.plain_text: Why the air filter matters

text.content: The air filter is the first line of defence in a screw compressor. It captures airborne dust and particulates before they reach rotors, bearings, and seals. A clogged filter starves the compressor of air, raising energy use and risking internal contamination.

rich_text.plain_text: The air filter is the first line of defence in a screw compressor. It captures airborne dust and particulates before they reach rotors, bearings, and seals. A clogged filter starves the compressor of air, raising energy use and risking internal contamination.

text.content: Step-by-step checklist

rich_text.plain_text: Step-by-step checklist

text.content: Turn off the compressor and depressurise the system before opening the housing.

rich_text.plain_text: Turn off the compressor and depressurise the system before opening the housing.

text.content: Lift the element out and inspect the media against a bright light — dark or oily media has reached end of life.

rich_text.plain_text: Lift the element out and inspect the media against a bright light — dark or oily media has reached end of life.

text.content: Clean the housing and intake path to prevent loose debris from entering the machine.

rich_text.plain_text: Clean the housing and intake path to prevent loose debris from entering the machine.

text.content: Replace the element with a genuine Kenrax replacement matched to your OEM part number.

rich_text.plain_text: Replace the element with a genuine Kenrax replacement matched to your OEM part number.

text.content: Reset the service-hour counter and log the change date for your maintenance records.

rich_text.plain_text: Reset the service-hour counter and log the change date for your maintenance records.

text.content: How often

rich_text.plain_text: How often

text.content: In dusty manufacturing floors, inspect every 500–1000 operating hours. In clean, climate-controlled facilities, elements often last 2000–4000 hours. When in doubt, replace it — a filter is far cheaper than a compressor that ingested abrasive dust.

title: When to Replace Your Compressor Oil Filter

text.content: The oil filter is a sacrificial component

rich_text.plain_text: The oil filter is a sacrificial component

text.content: The oil filter continuously removes carbon deposits, metal shavings, sludge, and particulate from the lubricating oil. Without it, those contaminants circulate through bearings, rotors, and seals and accelerate wear.

rich_text.plain_text: The oil filter continuously removes carbon deposits, metal shavings, sludge, and particulate from the lubricating oil. Without it, those contaminants circulate through bearings, rotors, and seals and accelerate wear.

text.content: Replacement intervals

rich_text.plain_text: Replacement intervals

text.content: For most oil-injected screw compressors, the filter is changed with the oil every 2000–4000 operating hours. Heavy-duty service or a dusty environment shortens that interval. Always follow the OEM schedule in your compressor manual, and never reuse a filter with fresh oil.

title: 5 Signs Your Air-Oil Separator Needs Replacing

text.content: Why separator health matters

rich_text.plain_text: Why separator health matters

text.content: The air-oil separator removes oil from the compressed air stream. A failing separator raises oil consumption, contaminates downstream equipment, and risks rejected product.

rich_text.plain_text: The air-oil separator removes oil from the compressed air stream. A failing separator raises oil consumption, contaminates downstream equipment, and risks rejected product.

text.content: The five warning signs

rich_text.plain_text: The five warning signs

text.content: Oil carryover at the discharge — oil mist in the air line or downstream of the aftercooler.

rich_text.plain_text: Oil carryover at the discharge — oil mist in the air line or downstream of the aftercooler.

text.content: Rising oil consumption with no external leak — oil is being pushed out with the air.

rich_text.plain_text: Rising oil consumption with no external leak — oil is being pushed out with the air.

text.content: Higher pressure drop across the separator — a loaded element restricts airflow and wastes energy.

rich_text.plain_text: Higher pressure drop across the separator — a loaded element restricts airflow and wastes energy.

text.content: Visible oil in condensate drains from the receiver or aftercooler.

rich_text.plain_text: Visible oil in condensate drains from the receiver or aftercooler.

text.content: Elapsed service interval — separators typically run 4000–8000 hours depending on duty and air quality.

rich_text.plain_text: Elapsed service interval — separators typically run 4000–8000 hours depending on duty and air quality.
